_comment: Rule pack. Conditions are declarative so detection engineers can tune rules without touching code. Severities follow docs/02-risk-scoring.md.

rules.title: Reads incoming SMS and has internet access
rules.description: The app can read or send text messages and can reach the network.
rules.rationale: One-time passwords arrive by SMS. This combination is the core of OTP theft and premium-SMS fraud, and is rarely needed by apps that are not messaging clients.

rules.title: Requests accessibility-service control
rules.description: The app can register a service that reads the screen and acts on the user's behalf.
rules.rationale: Accessibility access is the most abused Android permission: it enables keylogging, screen scraping and click automation, including tapping through permission and payment dialogs.

rules.title: Accessibility control combined with draw-over-other-apps
rules.description: The app can draw windows over other apps and automate the interface.
rules.rationale: Overlays plus accessibility is the classic banking-trojan pattern: a fake login screen is drawn while automation reads and submits real credentials.

rules.title: Can install other applications
rules.description: The app can prompt the user to install additional APKs.
rules.rationale: Install requests are how droppers deliver a second-stage payload that was not in the analysed file.

rules.title: Requests device-administrator rights
rules.description: The app can become a device administrator.
rules.rationale: Device admin allows locking the screen, resetting the device and disabling uninstall, which is the basis of Android ransomware.

rules.title: Starts itself at boot with a long-running service
rules.description: The app restarts after reboot and can keep a foreground service running.
rules.rationale: Persistence across reboots is required by most spyware so collection survives a phone restart.

rules.title: Reads contacts or call logs and has internet access
rules.description: Personal contact or call-history data can leave the device.
rules.rationale: Bulk harvesting of contacts and call logs is a defining behaviour of spyware and loan-app extortion.

rules.title: Requests broad storage or package visibility
rules.description: The app asks to see all files or every installed package.
rules.rationale: Broad visibility is used to inventory the device, find banking apps and locate documents to exfiltrate.

rules.title: Requests usage-statistics access
rules.description: The app can read which apps the user opens and for how long.
rules.rationale: Usage access is surveillance data and is also used to time overlays against banking apps.

rules.title: Can record audio or camera and run persistently
rules.description: Microphone or camera access is combined with background execution.
rules.rationale: Recording sensors without a visible foreground use is a spyware capability; legitimate apps normally capture only while open.

rules.title: Tracks location in the background and can upload it
rules.description: Fine-grained location is collected while the app is not in use.
rules.rationale: Background location plus network access is the stalkerware pattern; few non-navigation apps need it.

rules.title: Sends SMS from code
rules.description: The DEX references SmsManager send methods.
rules.rationale: Programmatic SMS sending is used for premium-rate fraud and for silently forwarding intercepted messages.

rules.title: Loads code at runtime
rules.description: The DEX references a runtime class loader.
rules.rationale: Loading DEX at runtime lets the analysed file hide its real behaviour behind a downloaded or decrypted payload.

rules.title: Executes shell commands
rules.description: The DEX references process execution APIs.
rules.rationale: Shell execution is used for root attempts and to run bundled binaries; ordinary apps rarely need it.

rules.title: Exposes a JavaScript bridge in a WebView
rules.description: A WebView loads content with JavaScript and a native bridge enabled.
rules.rationale: Bridging JS into app code turns a hijacked page or injected prompt into native-code access.

rules.title: Uses weak or hardcoded cryptography
rules.description: ECB-mode ciphers are referenced in code.
rules.rationale: ECB ignores block position and is common in string-encryption routines and in hand-rolled payload encryption.

rules.title: Reads telephony identifiers
rules.description: The app reads device or subscriber identifiers.
rules.rationale: Persistent identifiers are used for device fingerprinting and to bind a victim to an account.

rules.title: Queries SMS, contacts or call-log providers
rules.description: Content-provider queries target personal messaging or contact stores.
rules.rationale: Direct provider queries bypass the user-facing UI and are how bulk data is scraped.

rules.title: Automates the interface through accessibility
rules.description: Accessibility events and global actions are both used.
rules.rationale: Reading events and issuing global actions is the machinery of automated click fraud and permission-dialog abuse.

rules.title: Can lock or wipe the device
rules.description: Device-administrator lock or wipe calls are present.
rules.rationale: Locking or wiping without a clear enterprise context is the defining action of Android ransomware.

rules.title: Reads the clipboard
rules.description: The app reads clipboard contents.
rules.rationale: Clipboards carry passwords, OTPs and crypto addresses; reading them is a cheap credential-theft path.

rules.title: Inventories installed apps and can upload the list
rules.description: The package list is combined with network capability.
rules.rationale: App inventories are used to decide which banking or wallet apps a victim has installed.

rules.title: Resolves methods and fields by reflection
rules.description: Classes are loaded by name and members resolved at runtime.
rules.rationale: Reflection hides API use from simple scanners and is common in droppers and packed loaders.

rules.title: Combines Base64, crypto and a class loader
rules.description: Decoding, decryption and dynamic loading appear together.
rules.rationale: That three-step chain is a payload-unpacking routine: decode a blob, decrypt it, load it as code.

rules.title: Contacts a raw IP address or non-standard port
rules.description: A URL points at a numeric address instead of a domain.
rules.rationale: Hardcoded IPs avoid domain takedowns and are typical of disposable command-and-control endpoints.

rules.title: Ships a Telegram or Discord exfiltration endpoint
rules.description: A chat-service bot endpoint is embedded in the app.
rules.rationale: Bot APIs are free, anonymous and instant: the standard way malware ships stolen data off-device.

rules.title: Allows cleartext HTTP traffic
rules.description: HTTP is explicitly allowed or used.
rules.rationale: Cleartext traffic exposes credentials and stolen data to network attackers, and is unusual in maintained apps.

rules.title: Uses disposable or anonymised infrastructure
rules.description: A URL uses dynamic DNS, a tunnel, a paste site or Tor.
rules.rationale: These services are free and fast to rotate, which is why they host short-lived malware infrastructure.

rules.title: Contains a hardcoded cloud credential
rules.description: An AWS or Google API key pattern appears in the DEX strings.
rules.rationale: Committed keys give backend access to anyone who extracts them and confirm the app talks to owned infrastructure.

rules.title: Signed with a debug or expired certificate
rules.description: The signing certificate is a debug key or has expired.
rules.rationale: Debug keys are excluded by Play and shared by every development build; expired certs signal an abandoned or repackaged app.

rules.title: Insecure build flags
rules.description: The manifest marks the app debuggable or test-only.
rules.rationale: Debuggable builds allow attached debugging and memory inspection, and are not production releases.

rules.title: Known packer or protector detected
rules.description: Signatures of a commercial Android packer are present.
rules.rationale: Packers hide the real DEX from static analysis; a low score on a packed app means little and the report says so.

rules.title: Ships a hidden second-stage payload in assets
rules.description: An asset looks like packed code or a high-entropy blob.
rules.rationale: Executable or encrypted assets are where droppers keep the payload before loading it at runtime.

rules.title: Exports components without protecting them
rules.description: At least one exported component has no permission guard.
rules.rationale: Any app on the device can invoke these entry points; when they perform sensitive work this is a hijack path.

rules.title: Declares an accessibility service
rules.description: A service named as an accessibility service is declared.
rules.rationale: Combined with BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE this is an active screen-control implementation, not just a requested permission.

rules.title: Declares a notification listener
rules.description: The app implements a notification listener service.
rules.rationale: Notification access exposes one-time passcodes and bank alerts shown by other apps.

rules.title: Registers for incoming SMS broadcasts
rules.description: A receiver is registered for the incoming-SMS broadcast.
rules.rationale: Receiving that broadcast is a precondition for intercepting verification codes before the user sees them.

combos.title: Banking-trojan pattern
combos.rationale: Screen control, draw-over windows, SMS access and a network path together describe a banking trojan campaign rather than isolated risky permissions.

combos.title: One-time-passcode interception pattern
combos.rationale: Reading incoming SMS while listening for the broadcast, with no visible messaging purpose, is how OTPs are harvested.

combos.title: Second-stage dropper pattern
combos.rationale: Install capability plus runtime DEX loading plus a shipped blob means the analysed file is only the first stage.

combos.title: Ransomware pattern
combos.rationale: Device-admin rights, lock or wipe calls and boot persistence are the standard Android ransomware chain.

combos.title: Stalkerware pattern
combos.rationale: Background location combined with reboot persistence and upload capability describes covert tracking.

combos.title: Bulk personal-data harvesting
combos.rationale: Contacts or call logs plus SMS plus a network path is bulk collection of the data spyware sells.

combos.title: Notification interception with exfiltration
combos.rationale: A notification listener plus an embedded exfiltration endpoint lets the app forward 2FA codes in real time.
